WHY MICROSOFT WINS  ·  END-TO-END COVERAGE
Microsoft’s estate-native reach — Sentinel, Defender, Purview, Entra and Intune under one identity and data fabric — feeds every agent 
first-party signal across email, endpoint, identity, cloud and data. That shared context lets the agents triage, correlate and remediate 
across the full attack surface out of the box, so each new agent inherits the same enriched telemetry. CrowdStrike’s agents stay endpoint-
rooted and meter Charlotte AI credits — and its SOC still has no native email security or its own identity provider.

FAST ANSWERS FOR SELLERS
What is Project Perception?
Microsoft’s coordinated, multi-agent defense system: signals, 
context, models and specialized agents work together to reason, 
prioritize and act — with humans in control.
How do the agents work together?
Playbooks assign Red, Blue and Green agents shared objectives. 
Agents exchange findings and request approvals as they expose, 
investigate and close security gaps.
What do Red / Blue / Green agents do?
Red identifies paths to compromise. Blue investigates context, 
triages alerts and improves detections. Green prioritizes 
remediation and hardens posture.
How is it different from Security Copilot?
Security Copilot is the generative AI assistant for chat, skills and 
promptbooks. Perception is a multi-agent defense system for 
coordinated, multi-step workflows.
Why Microsoft vs. Charlotte AI?
Lead with closed-loop defense and Microsoft security context. 
Perception coordinates across Defender-first workflows; Charlotte 
AI generally stays inside Falcon-centric workflows.
Can customers access it now?
Preview is targeted and starts in Microsoft Defender. Use 
approved assets and demos; tell interested customers Microsoft 
will share availability as preview scales.

Playbooks assign Red, Blue and Green agents shared objectives.

promptbooks. Perception is a multi-agent defense system for 
coordinated, multi-step workflows.

Secure Foundations / Get Ready for AI
Exposure management becomes the organizing layer for proactive security.
CrowdStrike: Expanded exposure management by combining ExPRT.AI, Falcon intelligence
and XM Cyber attack paths to rank risk by exploitability, reachability and business impact. The
proof point is graph depth across cloud, network and unmanaged assets.
Palo Alto Networks: Expanded Cortex and Unit 42 services to correlate asset, vulnerability,
identity and threat context, validate attack paths and move prioritized risk into remediation
across endpoint, network and cloud.
Google/Wiz: Launched an MSP program around the Wiz Security Graph, which links cloud
configuration, vulnerabilities, identities, secrets, data and network exposure. Google and Wiz
still need to prove unified telemetry, policy and response.
Zscaler: Expanded exposure management by combining Zero Trust traffic, identity, inline
policy and Symmetry data telemetry to identify risky access paths and block sessions.
Coverage remains strongest where traffic traverses Zscaler.


--- PAGE 5 ---
Implications for Microsoft: Lead with Microsoft Security Exposure Management as the cross-
domain layer connecting identity, endpoint, cloud, email, code and Microsoft 365 signals to critical
assets, attack paths and remediation. Use MDASH to extend the story upstream: validated code
findings can be tied to deployed assets and real-world risk, then tracked through remediation and
verification using controls customers already own
React to section
Securing Data
Data security is converging with AI security and agent access.
Proofpoint: Announced Agentic Data and AI Security and Agentic Collaboration Security,
using its Knowledge Graph to correlate behavior, messages, data sensitivity and AI intent.
Policies can coach, block or investigate risk, but core capabilities remain staged through Q1
2027.
Varonis: Launched Data Lifecycle Management to identify stale, redundant and overexposed
content using sensitivity and access context, then drive disposition or remediation. Buyers
should test repository coverage, policy precision and records safeguards.
Okta, SailPoint and CrowdStrike: Their agent-identity announcements move data policy
closer to runtime: identity establishes the actor, authorization limits tools and resources, and
data controls govern what agents can read, create, retain or share.
Implications for Microsoft: Lead with Purview as the policy and enforcement layer across data at
rest, in use and in motion, with shared classification, DSPM for AI, DLP and audit across Microsoft
365, endpoints, browsers, SaaS, the network and agent traffic. Pair it with Entra Global Secure
Access to show how identity and sensitivity context can block risky human and agent activity before
data leaves, while auto-labeling, eDiscovery and lifecycle controls extend governance at scale.

Monthly Security Compete Bulletin - October
2026
 Sent to scicompetenews@microsoft.com  Subscribe | Unsubscribe
Time to read: about 9 minutes.
October made one thing clear: the AI security contest has moved from finding agents to stopping them.
Competitors want to be the neutral control layer across Copilot, Foundry, Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Bedrock and
Gemini, but much of what they offer is gateway-only, in preview or still on the roadmap. In deals, ask one question:
what can you stop and revoke today?
Recent Research & Content
Agent 365 Battlecard - Placemats rescored for ten competitors(Google and Wiz shown
as one); agent discovery rows now includes local agents, roadmap badges added, every
mark sourced. Differentiators, objection handling and FAQs updated.
Agentic SOC Battlecards CrowdStrike & Google - Added Google AI Threat Defense, Wiz
Atlas, AI SAST, agent updates & CrowdStrike Fal.Con 2026 news. FrontierCo positioing
and ISOC added.
Defend with AI Battlecard - Update with cyber stack comparison slides.
ServiceNow Security Battlecard - Rebuilt for the Agent 365/E7 upsell, now covering
ServiceNow's September 2026 release. New: head-to-head matrix with ServiceNow
entitlement codes, control-point comparison, coexistence models, defensibility table,
ServiceNow architecture and its scope beyond AI Control Tower. 
CrowdStrike Compete Playbook - Updates across CrowdStrike portfolio from endpoint to
Charlotte AI, with strengths, weaknesses and objections. Falcon bundle, discounting and
Flex tactics. Four key deal scenarios, best practices and Microsoft differentiators.

Key market insights
Agent security is moving from visibility to intervention: CrowdStrike, SailPoint, ServiceNow, Salesforce and
IBM have shipped or announced kill switches, runtime authorization and human approval gates since early
October. Most are narrower than the headlines: CrowdStrike's switch works through a gateway, SailPoint's and
IBM's are in preview, and Salesforce's triggered version lands in January 2027. Finding agents is now table
stakes; buyers will compare who can contain one.


--- PAGE 2 ---
Competitors are instrumenting Microsoft's AI surfaces: CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian added policy hooks in
Microsoft 365 Copilot and GitHub Copilot, CrowdStrike and SentinelOne are putting sensors in the Claude
Cowork virtual machine, and IBM now discovers and contains Microsoft Foundry agents. SentinelOne's Cowork
agent is still planned and IBM's capability is in tech preview.
Control-plane alliances are forming around Microsoft, not with it: ServiceNow's Control Tower Alliance
(Anthropic, AWS, Cisco, Okta, OpenAI, NVIDIA and others) and NVIDIA OpenShell (CrowdStrike, Palo Alto
Networks, Zscaler, Okta, ServiceNow) each want to be the neutral layer for governing enterprise AI.
Frontier cyber models are now a gated product category: OpenAI shipped GPT-6 and GPT-6 Cyber, Google
introduced Gemini 4 Carbon and Anthropic launched its Cyber Mission. Security vendors resell the results
through AI marketplaces, such as Palo Alto Networks on the OpenAI Marketplace and Cyera on the Claude
Marketplace.
Agentic attacks moved from research to incident reports: Microsoft (Storm-0940 and Storm-3358 using
ARTEX), CrowdStrike (four agentic threat actors), Wiz (AI-driven multi-cloud intrusions) and Trend Micro
(CyberStrikeAI, 44 agents) all documented AI agents carrying out real intrusions.
Securing AI
The agent control point is shifting to the endpoint and the runtime, and kill switches are now a checklist item.
CrowdStrike: At Fal.Con Europe (November 3-4), extended Falcon Guardian across agent, network and
endpoint layers, with hooks that inspect and block prompts and tool calls in Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub
Copilot, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and Cursor.
The new AI Kill Switch only cuts an agent's model access through Falcon AI Gateway or a connected third-party
gateway and blocks relaunch on a host; endpoint termination, permission revocation and SaaS or browser
containment are undated, and local-model agents are not addressed.
It also agreed to acquire Fiddler AI (agent observability) and Dreadnode (AI red teaming), both expected to
close in Q4 FY27. Agent Graph (October 30) scores agents 0-100 and traces prompts to endpoint actions;
CrowdStrike says Guardian runs at hundreds of organizations, with availability varying by capability.
ServiceNow: Announced AI Passport (October 15), a signed runtime credential for scoped delegation and
revocation planned for Q4 2026; made its Arc enterprise agent generally available (October 21), though NVIDIA
OpenShell enforcement for AI Passport comes in a later release; and launched the Control Tower Alliance
(October 28) to make Control Tower the cross-vendor AI control plane.
Palo Alto Networks: Launched Cortex XDR One (October 19), pairing XDR with Agentic Endpoint Security for AI-
agent inventory, runtime guardrails and endpoint-resident small language models, plus Unit 42 Managed
Agentic Endpoint Security for 24/7 oversight. It targets Defender for Endpoint directly; the 95% false-positive
reduction is vendor-reported.
SentinelOne: Put Singularity Agentic Detection and Response into early access (October 21) to discover agents
and stop unintended actions, and announced a planned runtime agent inside Claude Cowork (November 2).
SailPoint, Salesforce and IBM: At Navigate (October 5-8), SailPoint showed runtime authorization and an agent
kill switch for Agentic Fabric, both in preview; the kill switch has no GA date. Salesforce Agent Fabric made its
existing Agent Kill Switch generally available, but the Triggered-Agent Kill Switch is not due until January 2027.


--- PAGE 3 ---
IBM's watsonx Orchestrate Discover and Contain, for agents on Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry and Gemini, is in
tech preview.
Okta and Anthropic: Okta expanded its AWS agreement (November 5) and plans to explore Cross App Access
and verified human approval in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Anthropic made prompt and pre-tool-call hooks
generally available for Claude Enterprise and added a security center in beta.
Implications for Microsoft: Expect CrowdStrike, SentinelOne and SailPoint to tell customers they can stop agents,
including inside Copilot. Most of what they show is narrower than it sounds: gateway cutoffs, previews or features
with no GA date.
In deals, ask three questions. Can you revoke the agent's identity and access, not just its model connection? Does data
policy follow the agent? Is it shipping today? Microsoft's answer is that Agent 365, Entra Agent ID, Defender and
Purview discover, govern and stop agents across Microsoft and third-party estates. Back it up with the November 5
updates (Dynamic Permissions, Dynamic Agent Risk, Dynamic Conditional Access and generally available Execution
Containers for local agents) and the October 19 Microsoft 365 E7 and Project Perception capabilities that treat agents
as insiders. Be just as clear about what is GA versus preview on our side; customers will check.
Defend with AI
Frontier labs and cloud providers are turning AI vulnerability discovery and remediation into products.
OpenAI: Released GPT-6 (October 7) and GPT-6.1 Terra (October 26), which it says meets its Critical
cybersecurity threshold, then launched GPT-6 Cyber for approved Daybreak Red customers (November 5) with
a vendor-reported 48.5% on ExploitGym.
It expanded partnerships with ServiceNow (attack-path validation and mitigation, early access January 2027)
and Oracle (AI Security Mesh), and was reported to be in preliminary talks to acquire Trail of Bits.
Google: Introduced Gemini 4 Carbon (October 28), with vendor-reported scores of 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro and
54.8% on ExploitGym, initially only for a subset of cyber defenders. Google Cloud previewed CodeMender
isolation and human checks (November 4).
Anthropic: Launched the Cyber Mission (October 8), a long-term commitment to help defenders secure critical
infrastructure and open-source software. It includes a Critical Infrastructure Defense Program, with founding
partners including CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks. Anthropic also split its Cyber Verification Program into
three access tiers.
AWS: Made AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities generally available (October 22), but only in two US
regions; it validates exploitability, prioritizes by business impact and proposes fixes that need human approval.
AWS also says its Security Agent exploited 33 of 37 real-world CVEs in testing.
CrowdStrike and SentinelOne: CrowdStrike made coordinated multi-agent investigations generally available,
previewed agent insider threat detection for Q4 and put Agentic Adversary Emulation in early access
(November 4). SentinelOne unveiled Singularity ASOC (October 21), bundling AI SIEM, hyperautomation and AI
data pipelines with analyst-directed agentic investigations.
Implications for Microsoft: Customers will hear benchmark scores from OpenAI, Google and AWS, and agentic SOC
pitches from CrowdStrike and SentinelOne. Don't get pulled into a model-score contest: most of these models are


--- PAGE 4 ---
gated or in early access, and the figures are vendor claims. Move the conversation to what the AI can see, what it may
execute and who approves it. Microsoft's story: MDASH finds and proves vulnerabilities upstream, and Project
Perception runs governed investigation and response across Defender, Sentinel, Entra and Purview signals.
Get Ready for AI / Secure Foundation
SIEM displacement and exposure validation are the main pressure points on the core platform.
CrowdStrike: Partnered with Dynatrace (November 2) on federated search and log routing, pitched as a
cheaper alternative to legacy SIEM and aimed squarely at Microsoft Sentinel. It also added Third-Party IOC
Management to Falcon Next-Gen SIEM, made Falcon Seraphic Enterprise Browser native to Falcon, and added
real-time detection and response for Azure and Kubernetes plus container image supply-chain checks.
Palo Alto Networks: At InterSECt 2026 (October 8), introduced PAN-OS 12.2 with Frontier Virtual Patching and
Network Security Agents, and cited vendor-reported SecureIQLab NGFW and SSE results.
Google/Wiz: Wiz launched AI SAST (October 6) and AI Agents for Gov (October 14), and previewed a native Wiz
Runtime Sensor for GKE with Google Cloud (October 20).
Zscaler: Partnered with IBM and Red Hat on Autonomous Application Shield (October 5) to protect private apps
between disclosure and exploitation, and detailed AI-based Cloud Sandbox verdicts.
Proofpoint: Joined the Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Integrated Cloud Email Security ecosystem (October
26), with detections visible in the Defender portal, and launched Proofpoint Flex (October 28) so customers can
shift committed spend across its portfolio.
Implications for Microsoft: In SIEM deals, expect CrowdStrike to pair a data-cost argument, now backed by its
Dynatrace partnership, with product claims aimed at Sentinel. Answer with total cost and coverage, and show the
integrated Defender portal, where Sentinel, Defender XDR, Exposure Management and Security Copilot share
incidents, entities and response, with ISOC as the path to consolidating SecOps. When Proofpoint is in an email deal,
use its new Defender for Office 365 ICES integration to show that Defender stays the email security hub.
Securing Data
Data security is consolidating, and the combined vendors are targeting AI data exposure.
Proofpoint and Varonis: Proofpoint (owned by Thoma Bravo) agreed to acquire Varonis for about $6.3 billion in
cash (October 15), creating what it calls the largest data and AI security company, with 16,000+ enterprise
customers. The deal has not closed; it is expected to close in the first half of 2027, pending shareholder and
regulatory approvals.
Cyera: Added its AI Security Platform to the Anthropic Claude Marketplace (October 16). CTech reported on
November 9 that Cyera is negotiating a round of about $800 million at about a $20 billion valuation; nothing
has been announced.
Cyberhaven, Box and Sentra: Cyberhaven introduced an Agentic Data Security module for AI data flows and
Box made agent security controls generally available (both November 5); Sentra announced a $150 million
strategic investment led by Capital One Ventures (November 4).


--- PAGE 5 ---
Zscaler: Its October GovCloud update added Endpoint DLP for portable devices, real-time PDF OCR and Zoom AI
transcript scanning, several in limited availability.
Implications for Microsoft: Expect a combined Proofpoint and Varonis to pitch email, insider risk and data posture
under one owner, even though the deal has not closed and integration will take most of 2027. Ask customers how
they plan to run two separate products until then. Microsoft's answer is Purview as one classification and policy layer
across Microsoft 365, endpoints, browsers, SaaS and agent traffic, with DSPM for AI, DLP, Insider Risk Management
and audit built in where the data and agents already run. In active deals, use the Proofpoint's Acquisition of Varonis

What is Perception?
Applies to: Project Perception
Perception is a new multi-agent security system designed for the realities of AI. Perception brings
together signals, context, models, and specialized agents into a continuously learning system of
defense. It can reason, prioritize, and act at machine speed while keeping humans firmly in
control and empowering them with powerful new workflows.
Perception is based on a simple idea: effective defense requires continuously understanding how
an attacker sees the world, how a defender evaluates risk, and how protections are improved
over time.
Perception brings together three categories of specialized security agents: red team agents that
expose vulnerabilities before attackers can exploit them, blue team agents that detect, triage,
and investigate threats, and green team agents that remediate and harden your posture.
Working together, they form a closed-loop system that continuously discovers, evaluates, and
improves an organization's security posture.
For a full breakdown of each category and the agents within it, see Agent categories in
Perception.
Perception uses coordinated agent playbooks to achieve specific security outcomes. A playbook
assigns a team of specialized agents a set of objectives and orchestrates their actions throughout
the workflow. Each agent has a distinct role, but they work together by sharing intelligence,
findings, and security context to drive coordinated defense. Throughout the workflow, agents
surface recommendations and request approvals when needed, keeping security teams in control
of critical decisions.
To see how the agents work together in a complete workflow, see Agent categories in Perception.

Key concepts in Perception
Applies to: Project Perception
Perception uses the following concepts to organize agentic work: sessions, agents, and
playbooks. Understanding these concepts helps you configure, delegate, and supervise agentic
operations effectively.
A session is the record of an agent interaction. Sessions capture agent activity, decisions, inputs,
outputs, and any approvals or human interventions. Sessions can involve a single agent or
multiple agents working in coordination. Each session has a status that reflects the aggregate
state of all tasks within it.
For more information about sessions, see View and manage sessions.
An agent is an autonomous or semi-autonomous software entity that can reason, use tools, and
perform tasks. Perception agents are Microsoft-published agents designed for deep, autonomous
security operations work. They form the core of Microsoft's multi-agent SOC system, covering the
full security operations lifecycle from threat intelligence through detection authoring, exposure
analysis, posture prioritization, alert triage, and incident investigation.
Perception agents are designed to collaborate. The output from one agent becomes input for
another, enabling end-to-end workflows. For example, threat intelligence extracted by the Threat
Intelligence Agent feeds directly into detections created by the Detection Authoring Agent.
Perception agents require an agent identity and role assignment before they can be used. For
setup instructions, see Work with agents.

Use the Recon Agent in Project Perception
Applies to: Project Perception
The Recon Agent in Project Perception gives security teams and red team operators an attacker-
perspective view of an Azure environment. It correlates assets, identities, permissions, and
network exposure to identify realistic attack paths, configuration issues, and exposure risks
without changing resources.
Use this article to understand the Recon Agent's capabilities, review its prerequisites and
permissions, set it up, start a session, and interpret its report.
The Recon Agent runs multi-step, AI-orchestrated reconnaissance in your Azure environment.
Read-only assessment: Provides an evidence-backed risk assessment without changing
resources.
Input for other agents: Provides findings to other agents, including investigation agents.
Environment-grounded analysis: Analyzes only data from your Azure environment.
） Important

Key capabilities
７ Note
The Recon Agent creates a read-only assessment. It doesn't exploit vulnerabilities, execute
payloads, modify resources, deploy detections, persist attack graphs, or operate outside your
organization. The agent analyzes your environment through read-only API calls. Results are a
point-in-time snapshot and don't replace continuous monitoring systems.


--- PAGE 30 ---
Microsoft Security Exposure Management continuously identifies attack paths that originate from
internet-exposed assets, critical resources, and sensitive identities. It monitors these marked
assets and identities, but doesn't generate attack paths from arbitrary starting points that don't
meet these criteria.
The Recon Agent complements Exposure Management with assumed-breach analysis. Analysts
can start with any asset or identity in an Azure subscription. Assets don't need to be designated
as critical or internet exposed, and identities don't need to be marked as sensitive. The analysis
answers the question, "If an attacker already controlled this asset or identity, where could they go
next?"
For example, a phishing attack might compromise a user who isn't marked as a sensitive identity
in Defender. Exposure Management typically doesn't generate an attack path from that user
unless the path includes another marked asset. The Recon Agent can use the user as the starting
point to reveal potential attacker pivots. Teams can then identify effective choke points before
those paths lead to incidents involving critical resources or sensitive identities.
This broader starting-point coverage helps teams identify attack paths across their Azure
environment and prioritize critical paths in time to reduce security operations center (SOC)
incident volume.

visibility

Explains whether an alert or finding is part of a broader attacker route and what

Attack path analysis
Runs targeted, session-based reconnaissance scoped to a subscription, resource
group, or critical asset and can reason over missing data, failed steps, and
inferred paths.

Maps attack-path steps to existing Defender alerts and hunting coverage, then
highlights where the SOC may lack visibility.

Triage Agent
Applies to: Project Perception
Security Operations Centers (SOCs) process large volumes of alerts in multiple workloads, and
each workload requires different context, signals, and investigative depth. Differences in how
analysts evaluate these alerts can lead to inconsistent triage decisions and slow the ability to
distinguish real threats from false alarms. As a result, high-risk activity can be missed or delayed,
while analysts spend disproportionate time filtering noise instead of acting on what matters
most.
The Triage Agent is an autonomous agent embedded in Microsoft Defender that helps security
teams triage alerts at scale. It applies AI-driven, dynamic reasoning over evidence to deliver clear
verdicts for supported security workloads. By identifying which alerts represent real attacks and
which are false positives, the agent enables analysts to focus on investigating real threats, with
transparent, step-by-step reasoning to support every decision.
The Triage Agent classifies and triages alerts in Microsoft Defender for supported workloads and
alert types. The agent's key capabilities include:
Autonomous triage: Uses advanced AI tools to evaluate alerts and determine whether they
represent malicious activity or false alarms without requiring step-by-step human input.
Transparent rationale: Records classification verdicts and provides supporting reasoning in
natural language and visual graphs, including the evidence used to reach each conclusion.
Learning based on feedback: For supported alert types, the agent can incorporate analyst
feedback when explicitly provided and approved to tune its verdict analysis. This capability

further action.

corresponding incident.

Lessons provide systematic guidelines that help the agent determine whether an alert is a
genuine phishing threat or a false alarm. To ensure the agent effectively incorporates your
feedback, follow these best practices when providing input to the Triage Agent:
1. Ensure feedback is relevant and contextual. Feedback should pertain only to the email
currently under review. It must also align with the updated classification you assign.
2. Be descriptive and specific. Clearly explain the characteristics of the email. Provide relevant
details like the email subject, message body, sender, or recipients to help the agent
understand the context. Specific feedback with multiple details enhances effectiveness.
3. Ensure clarity and decisiveness. Avoid vague or universal statements. Give feedback that's
clear and actionable. Use decisive and clear identification terms.
4. Be consistent with previous feedback. Ensure that new feedback aligns with what you
previously provided to avoid contradictions that could confuse the agent or reduce the
accuracy of its decisions. You can review all previously submitted input on the Feedback
management page.
5. Review the agent's interpretation of your feedback. When you submit feedback, always
verify that the feedback is accurately translated into a lesson. Confirm that the lesson
reflects your intent and maintains consistency with your original input. Check the validity of
AI-generated responses to ensure they're applicable to the scenario.

You can trigger this agent playbook manually. The agent runs automatically when a new alert is
detected. The setup process disables built-in tuning rules that resolve supported alert types.
Microsoft AI agents follow strict Responsible AI guidelines and undergo thorough reviews to
ensure compliance with all AI standards and safeguards. The Triage Agent is fully incorporated
into these controls. During setup, you assign the agent an identity and configure it with the
minimum permissions required for its operation, ensuring that it doesn't have unnecessary
permissions. The system logs all agent activities in detail, and analysts and admins can review the
complete flow at any time. The system logs feedback provided to the agent to help it adapt to
the organization's environment. Admins can review and modify this feedback as needed.
While both SOAR solutions and the Triage Agent automate aspects of security operations, they
use different approaches.
SOAR solutions typically rely on predefined, rule-based workflows that require manual
configuration and ongoing maintenance. In contrast, the Triage Agent uses reasoning-based
analysis to triage alerts and record classifications within Defender, with human oversight and
optional feedback where supported.
The agent operates within defined permissions and workflows in Defender and doesn't replace
existing investigation or response tools.

The Attack Investigation Agent is an autonomous tier 2 investigator for security operations

investigation to ask questions or request deeper analysis.

Tenant-aware detection analysis and tuning


--- PAGE 97 ---
The agent identifies which tables and data sources are available in the tenant and bases its
recommendations on that data. This means every proposed detection is grounded in what your
environment actually collects, rather than assuming data availability that may not exist.
Detection simulation and noise estimation
For each proposed detection, the agent runs a simulation against historical tenant data and
reports the projected alert volume. This gives you an early indication of the detection's expected
coverage, potential noise level, and overall quality before you deploy it.
Automated tenant-specific tuning
Based on simulation results, the agent identifies detections likely to be noisy and automatically
suggests optimizations. By analyzing the generated alerts, it can detect recurring benign patterns
and refine the rule accordingly. For example, if a specific user, device, or application appears
frequently in simulated alerts and is assessed as benign, the agent may recommend excluding it
from the detection logic.
Based on the results and tenant-specific baselines, proposed detections are automatically
categorized into two groups:
Ready to deploy: Detections expected to be high quality and relatively low noise compared
to other custom detections in the environment. These can typically be enabled with minimal
additional review.
Requires tuning: Detections expected to generate a relatively high level of noise based on
simulation results and tenant-specific characteristics. The agent provides concrete
recommendations to improve their quality before deployment.
Detections proposed by the agent are tagged with a Provider value of Copilot. You can use this
property to filter and identify agent-generated detections in your custom detections list.

Microsoft's Application and Platform cards are intended to help you understand how our AI
technology works, the choices application owners can make that influence application
performance and behavior, and the importance of considering the whole application, including
the technology, the people, and the environment. Application cards are created for AI
applications and platform cards are created for AI platform services. These resources can support
the development or deployment of your own applications and can be shared with users or

As part of its commitment to responsible AI, Microsoft adheres to six core principles
: fairness,
reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, and accountability. These
principles are embedded in the Responsible AI Standard
, which guides teams in designing,
building, and testing AI applications. Application and Platform cards play a key role in
operationalizing these principles by offering transparency around capabilities, intended uses, and
limitations. For further insight, readers are encouraged to explore Microsoft's Responsible AI
Transparency Report
 and the Microsoft Enterprise AI Services Code of Conduct, which outlines
how to engage with AI responsibly.
Perception is a new multi-agent security system designed for the realities of AI. Perception brings
together signals, context, models, and specialized agents into a continuously learning system of
defense. It can reason, prioritize, and act at machine speed while keeping humans firmly in
control and empowering them with powerful new workflows.
The intended users include SOC analysts, detection engineers, security architects, IT
administrators, and security leaders such as Chief Information Security Officers (CISOs). Both
traditional SOC teams and frontier security engineers who operate at scale across multiple
security domains can use Perception.

Perception agents use the underlying large language model to analyze available context, evaluate

Understanding the limitations of Perception is important to ensure it is used effectively and
responsibly. While Perception enhances security workflows, it isn't designed for every scenario.
Refer to the Microsoft Enterprise AI Services Code of Conduct as well as the following
considerations when choosing a use case:
Accuracy and completeness: Agents can produce responses that are inaccurate,
incomplete, or outdated. Output quality depends on the data sources available at runtime,
the permissions the administrator grants to the agent, and the quality of the input provided.
Apply human judgment and validate critical outputs before acting on them.
Domain-specific scope: Perception is optimized for security-related tasks such as threat
intelligence analysis, incident investigation, attack path mapping, and detection authoring.
Inputs outside this domain may result in less accurate or less relevant outputs.
Data source dependency: Agent outputs are grounded in available data, including
connected Microsoft Defender services and the agent's configured permissions. If relevant
data sources aren't available, enabled, or current, results may lack completeness or
accuracy.
Limitations


--- PAGE 146 ---
Agent setup required: Agents must be configured with an appropriate identity and
permissions before they can be used. Playbooks that include unconfigured agents aren't
available for use until all required agents are set up.
Azure environment scope: The Recon Agent analyzes Azure environments. Coverage is
limited to the Azure subscriptions and resources visible to the agent's configured identity.
Resources outside the agent's permission scope aren't analyzed.
Read-only reconnaissance: The Recon Agent operates in read-only mode. It doesn't modify,
exploit, or interact with the resources it analyzes. Its outputs are assessments and
recommendations, not automated remediations.
Approval gates and human oversight: Some agent actions require administrator or user
approval before the agent proceeds. This design is intentional. High-impact actions should
be reviewed by a human before execution.
Task-specific agent boundaries: Each agent is designed for a specific task. Agents aren't
suitable for tasks outside their defined scope and shouldn't be repurposed beyond their
intended use cases.
Preview status: Some capabilities in Perception may be in preview. Preview features should
be treated as prerelease functionality, and outputs should be reviewed before taking action.
Bias, stereotyping, and ungrounded content: Despite the implementation of responsible AI
controls, AI services are probabilistic. This makes it challenging to comprehensively block all
inappropriate content, which may lead to potential biases, stereotypes, or ungrounded
content in AI-generated outputs.

Approval gates: High-impact agent actions require explicit approval from a user or
administrator before the agent proceeds. This ensures that humans remain in control of

Least-privilege identity: Agents operate with configured identities scoped to the minimum
permissions required for their task. Administrators choose the agent identity during setup,

Read-only reconnaissance: The Recon Agent is designed to analyze without acting. It

Perception is designed to keep humans in control of consequential decisions while enabling
agents to automate high-volume, time-intensive tasks. Human oversight is built into the system
at multiple levels:
Approval gates: Agents can be configured to pause and request approval before taking
high-impact actions. Users or administrators review the proposed action and can approve,
reject, or redirect the agent.
Session supervision: Users can monitor in-progress sessions through the Perception
Sessions view, which shows what each agent is doing, what it has produced, and whether
it's waiting for input.
Stop controls: Users can stop any in-progress session. Stopping a session terminates all
active agent tasks within it.
Transparent reasoning: Agents surface their reasoning in a process log within the session
view. Users can review the steps the agent took, the data it accessed, and the conclusions it
reached.
Role-based access controls: Administrators configure role-based access control for each
agent, controlling who can run agents, who can view session results, and who can configure
agent settings. This ensures that access to agentic capabilities aligns with organizational
security policies.

Evaluate legal and regulatory considerations: Customers need to evaluate potential
specific legal and regulatory obligations when using any AI platforms and solutions, which
may not be appropriate for use in every industry or scenario. Additionally, AI platforms or
solutions are not designed for and may not be used in ways prohibited in applicable terms
of service and relevant codes of conduct.

might still make mistakes. The outputs generated may be inaccurate, incomplete, biased,

such as ambiguity in the inputs or limitations of the underlying models. As such, users
should review the responses generated by Perception and verify that they match their
expectations and requirements.

application abandonment, financial loss, psychological harm, physical harm, among others.
(e.g. a doctor accepts an incorrect AI output). In Perception, overreliance could lead to
missed threats, incorrect incident conclusions, ineffective detection rules, or remediation of

reasoning or output doesn't match the intended goal.
Configure, test, and monitor Perception carefully: Grant each agent access only to the data
and actions required for its defined task. Before broad deployment, test playbooks with
representative scenarios and confirm that approval gates and user controls work as
expected. Introduce autonomy gradually, train users on agent limitations, and regularly
review session records, feedback, and security outcomes for changes in quality or behavior.
Provide feedback when issues arise: Microsoft continuously improves Perception based on
customer feedback and operational data. To provide feedback on agent performance or
report unexpected behavior, use the feedback controls available in the session view after an
agent completes its work.
For additional guidance or to learn more about the responsible use of Perception, we
recommend reviewing the following documentation:

Overview  
 
 
Q1. What is ISOC in Defender? 
A.  ISOC in Microsoft Defender brings together leading SIEM and threat protection in an integrated 
experience for agentic security, giving people and agents a shared foundation to see, understand, 
and act across the environment without the complexity of operating separate systems. With SIEM 
capabilities directly integrated into Defender, customers can use SIEM capabilities on Defender data 
without re-ingestion, retain Defender data for 90 days by default, and flexibly extend retention and 
cost-effectively expand security coverage with 500+ connectors as their needs evolve. 
 
• 
Built for agentic security: Shared signals, context, and controls deliver the sensors and 
actuators that enable people and agents to perceive, reason, and act together. 
• 
Integrated protection loop: Connects pre-breach protection with post-breach detection 
and response through unified, threat-led workflows. 
• 
Designed for practitioners: A unified experience, system, and data model that brings 
people and agents together in the flow of work. 
 
ISOC is a benefit, not a standalone product.  
 
Q2. How does ISOC enable agentic security? 
A. ISOC provides the signals, context, and actuators that power agentic security. Signals help agents 
perceive what’s happening, context grounds their reasoning, and actuators enable them to take 
action. This shared foundation allows people and agents to work together across security 
operations while keeping practitioners in control of critical decisions.  
 
 
 


--- PAGE 5 ---
Microsoft Confidential | Internal Only 
 
Q3. How does ISOC strengthen Microsoft’s competitive positioning? 
A. ISOC strengthens Microsoft’s position by combining the breadth of Microsoft’s broad signals with 
integrated security operations, built in value, and a foundation for agentic security. 
• 
Unmatched security context: Microsoft brings broad native security signals, context, and 
controls endpoint, office, identity and cloud into the security operations foundation, that 
competitors can't easily replicate.  
• 
Integrated security operations: ISOC brings native threat protection, SIEM capabilities, 
and a foundation for agentic security in one integrated experience, delivering immediate 
security value from day one. 
• 
Better ROI: Built-in SIEM capabilities, 90 days of included retention for eligible Defender 
data, and cost-effective ingestion of additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security data at 
$2.40/GB helps customers maximize the value of their Microsoft investments. 
• 
Strengthens E3-to-E5 upsell conversations: ISOC expands the Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 
value proposition from threat protection to integrated security operations, giving 
customers another reason to consolidate more of their security stack on Microsoft.  
• 
Creates a differentiated path to agentic security: ISOC provides the foundation for 
security teams and Perception agents to work together on a common set of signals, context, 
and workflows, enabling faster investigations, coordinated response, and better security 
outcomes. 
Our differentiation is not simply SIEM plus XDR—it's an integrated security operations platform 
that delivers greater value today while laying the foundation for the agentic SOC of tomorrow. To 
learn more, see Defend with AI battlecard. 
Q4. Who is eligible for ISOC? 
A. ISOC is available to organizations with eligible Defender Suite, Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 licenses, 
with or without Microsoft Sentinel across commercial and government offerings. 
 
 


--- PAGE 6 ---
Microsoft Confidential | Internal Only 
 
Q5. Who is not eligible for ISOC? 
A.  
• 
Education, Frontline, and standalone Defender licenses customers are not eligible. 
• 
Sentinel customers who onboarded to the Sentinel data lake before September 23, 2026, 
cannot currently opt into ISOC. We will provide details on eligibility timelines and opt-in 
guidance in the coming weeks.   
Q6. What are we announcing at Ignite on November 17th? 
A. Core capabilities from Phase 1 of ISOC are now generally available (GA). Phase 2 makes the full 
breadth of SIEM capabilities now available in ISOC and expands eligibility to Sentinel customers. 
• 
ISOC phase 1 capabilities: Case management, workbooks, NL playbook generator, UEBA, 
CI/CD, Content hub (connectors) are now GA in ISOC. 
• 
Expanded customer eligibility: Eligible Defender Suite, Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 
customers with existing Sentinel workspaces can choose to opt into ISOC.  
• 
90-day Defender data retention: 90 days of default retention for eligible Defender data. 
• 
Built-in data lake: The lake tier is built into the ISOC workspace with no additional 
onboarding or subscription setup required. Customers can ingest data into the lake directly 
and configure data retention in Table Management. 
• 
Extended retention: Ability to extend eligible Defender data retention beyond the default 
period to 180 days, with a new $1.20/GB meter (meter goes LIVE on November 17th). 
Beyond 180 days, retain data in the analytics tier for up to two years or use long-term 
retention in the data lake for longer-term analysis, audit, or compliance needs. 
• 
Full SIEM capabilities: All Microsoft Sentinel SIEM capabilities will light-up in Defender, 
including SOC Optimization and Content Hub. 
• 
Sentinel migration tools: In-product migration tooling for custom detections, automation, 
and workbooks. See user guide for more details: https://aka.ms/ISOC_Sentinel_UserGuide. 
Q7. What changes for an existing Sentinel customer who opts into ISOC in terms of billing 
and commercial terms? 
A. Opting to ISOC is permanent and can’t be undone.  
• 
Discounts: Negotiated Sentinel discounts do not automatically transfer to ISOC and will 
need to be renegotiated with the Account Teams. 
• 
Billing: Applicable ISOC meters replace the corresponding Sentinel meters. 
• 
Commitment tiers:  Existing Sentinel commitment tiers do not carry over. ISOC ingestion is 
billed on a pay-as-you-go basis at $2.4 per GB. 
• 
5MB benefit: The 5MB per day Sentinel benefit is no longer applicable and is replaced by 
the ISOC benefit. 
• 
Dedicated clusters: Existing cluster commitments remain in place. However, ISOC usage is 
billed separately and does not count toward your existing dedicated cluster commitment. 
Unused capacity will be billed. 
 
[Note: The 5 MB/day Microsoft Sentinel benefit and Defender for Servers P2 benefit remain 
available to Sentinel customers who do not opt in to ISOC.]

Q9. How should customers think about Sentinel, Defender and ISOC going forward?  
A.   
• Microsoft Sentinel remains our leading SIEM solution and will continue to be available as a  
standalone purchase.  
• Microsoft Defender remains the threat protection foundation, providing protection,  
detection, investigation, and response across identities, endpoints, email, collaboration,  
SaaS, and cloud.  
• ISOC, or Integrated Security Operations Center, is an industry term that Gartner describes as 
an integrated, single-vendor approach to threat detection, investigation, and response.  
• 
ISOC in Microsoft Defender is not a new product. 
• 
It is a commercial option that brings Sentinel SIEM capabilities to eligible Defender 
customers, simplifying how customers get access to leading threat protection and SIEM 
capabilities in the Defender portal.  
• 
Through the ISOC benefit, eligible customers gain access to SIEM, XDR, threat intelligence, 
automation, and AI capabilities in Defender, helping them get more value from their existing 
Defender suites, Microsoft 365 E5, and Microsoft 365 E7 investments.

A. Sellers should lead with ISOC for every SOC opportunity while preserving customer choice for 
existing Sentinel customers. Guidance varies by customer scenario.

Q12. Is there an ME5 and ME7 seat threshold for ISOC eligibility? 
A. No. There is no minimum seat requirement. A tenant is eligible with any number of active 
Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E7, or Microsoft Defender Suite licenses. 
Q13. What customer roles are needed to onboard to ISOC?

Access Administrator + Sentinel Contributor). 
Q14. What data sources and tables are included in ISOC benefit with 90 days default

Q15. When will ISOC be available in Gov clouds? 
A. ISOC will be available in Gov clouds (GCC, GCCH, DOD) in Feb 2027 (GA). 
Q16. When will ISOC phase 2 capabilities be generally available? 
A. ISOC phase 2 will be generally available on January 15, 2027. 
Q17. Where is ISOC customer data stored and processed? 
A. An ISOC workspace follows the same data residency and retention behavior as an Azure Log 
Analytics workspace. 
Q18. What Sentinel capabilities are available in ISOC? 
A. All SIEM capabilities are available as part of the ISOC benefit starting Ignite.  
• 
Several capabilities are available out of the box without requiring a workspace.  
• 
An ISOC workspace is needed for additional data ingestion, extended retention, and certain 
advanced SIEM capabilities.

Q19. Does ISOC support dedicated clusters and CMK? 
A. Yes. 
• 
Dedicated-cluster-connected workspaces can continue to be used, with cluster 
management in Azure Log Analytics. However, ISOC ingestion does not decrement the 
existing cluster daily commitment. 
• 
Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) is supported in ISOC through the underlying Azure Log 
Analytics workspace.  
Q20. Does NL playbook generator require Microsoft Security Copilot license or Security 
Compute Units (SCUs)? 
A. No. It doesn't require a separate Microsoft Security Copilot license or SCUs. 
Q21. Does ISOC support multi-tenant security operations (MTO) and MSSP-managed 
environments? 
A. Yes. ISOC supports MSSP and multi-tenant security operations. MSSPs can transition Sentinel-
managed customer environments to ISOC while continuing to manage security operations across 
multiple customer tenants.  
Key considerations include: 


--- PAGE 11 ---
Microsoft Confidential | Internal Only 
 
• 
Multi-tenant operations: MSSPs can continue managing security operations across 
customer tenants, including case management, hunting, content, and other supported multi-
tenant workflows.  
• 
Content management: When transitioning to ISOC, MSSPs should review existing 
detections, workbooks, automation, Content Hub content, repositories, and CI/CD processes 
and update them for the ISOC experience where needed. 
• 
Access and permissions: MSSPs must validate delegated access and required permissions 
in each customer tenant. Unified RBAC and GDAP requirements depend on the workloads 
and operations being managed.  
• 
Transition planning: Before transitioning, MSSPs should identify existing Sentinel content, 
content-distribution/CI/CD processes, and shared content ownership, then validate that 
analysts retain access after the transition 
Refer to the playbook for more information: https://aka.ms/ISOC_playbook. 
 
 
 
Sentinel customers 
 
Q22. Are all Sentinel customers eligible to opt into ISOC starting at Ignite? 
A. No. Existing Sentinel customers who onboarded to the data lake before September 23, 2026, 
cannot currently opt in to ISOC. More details on eligibility and next steps will be shared in the 
coming weeks.  
Q23. Are all eligible Sentinel customers required to move to ISOC? 
A. No. ISOC opt-in is completely optional, with no forced move.  
• 
Customers should evaluate economic benefits of ISOC against their existing Sentinel 
investments and commercial terms before deciding whether to opt in.  
• 
Customers who choose not to opt in can continue using their existing Sentinel 
deployment as today. 
• 
The capabilities available in Microsoft Sentinel and ISOC workspaces are the same. 
Q24. Why should an existing Sentinel customer consider moving to ISOC? 
A. Moving to ISOC is optional. Customers should work with their account teams to evaluate the 
benefits against their existing Sentinel pricing, discounts, and operational needs. Customers can 
continue using Sentinel if it remains the better fit. 
 
ISOC offers: 
• 
Included Microsoft security data: Defender security data included with ISOC can help 
offset approximately 15–22% of net ingestion volume, depending on the customer's data 
mix. 
• 
Defender data retention: Get 90 days of Defender data retention included, without paying 
to re-ingest that data. 


--- PAGE 12 ---
Microsoft Confidential | Internal Only 
 
• 
Lower ingestion costs: Ingest additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft data from 500+ 
connectors at $2.40 per GB, potentially reducing costs for customers without significant 
existing Sentinel discounts. 
• 
Unified SOC experience: Bring security operations and threat protection together in 
Microsoft Defender to simplify investigation and response. 
Q25. What steps are required for existing Sentinel customers to opt-in to ISOC? 
A. Refer to the user guide for details: https://aka.ms/ISOC_Sentinel_UserGuide    
 
Q26. Can customers roll back to Sentinel after opting into ISOC? 
A. Opting into ISOC is permanent and can’t be undone. Sentinel customers should carefully evaluate 
technical readiness, billing implications, and commercial terms before proceeding. 
Q27. What should Sentinel customers still using the Azure portal do? 
A. Customers still operating Sentinel in the Azure portal should begin planning their transition to 
the Defender portal as Sentinel will no longer be supported in the Azure portal after March 31, 
2027. Once connected to the Defender portal, customers can opt in to ISOC. 
Q28. Will ISOC and Sentinel have the same features? 
A. Yes. ISOC brings Sentinel's SIEM capabilities into the Defender experience. Existing Sentinel 
customers can continue using Sentinel, with support for ISOC opt-in based on their needs. 
Q29. How can a customer who onboarded to the lake before September 23 get ISOC? 
A. A customer who onboarded to the Sentinel data lake before September 23, 2026, can request to 
offboard by creating a case through the support portal or working with their CSAM Account 
Manager.  
• 
Before offboarding, all lake-only tables must be removed or moved back to the 
Analytics tier. 
• 
The request is routed to the provisioning team, and offboarding typically takes up to 72 
hours once the request is assigned to the team.  
• 
After offboarding, the customer will have Sentinel with the built-in lake tier and, if eligible, 
can proceed with the ISOC upgrade.  
 
Important! Offboarding is irreversible. Customers who want to retain the data they currently have 
in the lake, should not use this path and should wait for migration guidance to the built-in lake. 


--- PAGE 13 ---
Microsoft Confidential | Internal Only 
 
 
Data tiers, ingestion, storage and analytics 
 
Q30. What are the two data tiers in ISOC? 
A. ISOC provides flexible data tier options across Analytics and data lake tiers to balance 
performance, retention, and cost. 
• 
Analytics tier: Provides real-time monitoring, alerts and full analytics for detections, 
investigations, and hunting.   
• 
Data lake tier: For cost-effective, long-term retention up to 12 years and historical 
analytics. 
Q31. What data ingestion and retention options are in ISOC? 
A. Customers get 90 days default retention for Defender data. Beyond the default period, ISOC 
offers flexible ingestion and retention options for Defender and non-Microsoft data across the 
Analytics and built-in data lake tiers.  
 
ISOC Defender data: 
• 
90 days of included retention: ISOC eligible data is available natively in Defender with 90 
days of included retention, without additional ingestion charges or requiring a workspace. 
• 
Extended Defender retention: Customers can extend select Defender data retention from 
90 to 180 days at $1.20/GB. New data is dual-ingested into an ISOC Analytics tier 
workspace; historical data is not backfilled. 
• 
Additional retention options: Through Table Management, customers can configure:  
o Extended interactive retention in the analytics tier at $0.10/GB/month, for up to 
two years. 
o Long-term storage in the lake at $0.026/GB/month. 
• 
Direct-to-lake ingestion: At any time, Defender data can be ingested directly into the data 
lake at $0.15/GB, with long-term storage at $0.026/GB/month. 
 
Additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft data: 
• 
Analytics ingestion with 90-day retention: Customers can ingest additional Microsoft 
and non-Microsoft security data into an ISOC workspace at $2.40/GB, including 90 days of 
Analytics tier retention. 
• 
Extended Analytics retention: Customers can retain data beyond 90 days for interactive 
investigations at $0.10/GB/month, for up to two years. 
• 
Long-term Data Lake retention: Through Table Management, customers can configure:  
o Extended interactive retention in the analytics tier at $0.10/GB/month, for up to 
two years. 
o Long-term storage in the lake at $0.026/GB/month. 
• 
Direct-to-lake ingestion: Customers can ingest data directly into the built-in data lake at 
$0.15/GB, with long-term storage at $0.026/GB/month. 


--- PAGE 14 ---
Microsoft Confidential | Internal Only 
 
 
 
 
[Note: An ISOC workspace is required to extend retention, additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft 
data ingestion.] 
 
Q32. What are the benefits of the built-in data lake tier? 
A. The built-in data lake enables customers to retain and analyze more security data at a lower cost. 
• 
The data lake is built in, with no additional onboarding or separate billing setup required. 
• 
Ingest data through 500+ connectors at a lower cost. 
• 
Data in the lake can be queried through Advanced Hunting. 
• 
Seamlessly mirror Analytics tier data to the lake at no additional cost. 
• 
Benefit from 6:1 data compression. 
• 
Build agents and advanced query scenarios via mirroring in Microsoft Fabric. 
Q33. In which regions is the built-in data lake available? 
A. Starting Ignite we are expanding the regions the data lake is available in. See documentation for 
the full list of supported regions.  
Q34. Will the built-in data lake be available in every Azure region, including Qatar Central? 
A. Not necessarily. Do not assume that availability in commercial-cloud regions means every Azure, 
sovereign, or government region will have the same availability. Some regions may require 
additional engineering or capacity validation due to dependencies on billing, or other supporting 
services.  
 
Qatar Central is one current example where additional validation is required. For customers in 
regions that are not listed as available, refer to the published regional availability documentation or 
contact ISOC Support to confirm availability before proceeding. 
 


--- PAGE 15 ---
Microsoft Confidential | Internal Only 
 
Q35. Do customers need to opt in to ISOC to use the built-in Sentinel data lake? 
A. No. Starting September 23, 2026, customers who were not already onboarded to the legacy 
Sentinel data lake get the built-in data lake when they create a Sentinel workspace. When an eligible 
customer opts in to ISOC, the same built-in lake foundation carries forward with the ISOC 
workspace. 
 
Q36. When do customers need Microsoft Fabric? 
A. Microsoft Fabric is optional and is primarily intended for customers that need advanced 
compute and analytics beyond day-to-day security operations in Microsoft Defender. Customers 
can use Fabric connection for scenarios such as notebooks, Spark jobs, data engineering, and data 
science to enrich, transform, and analyze security data. Most SOC analysts can continue their daily 
detection, investigation, hunting, and response workflows directly in Microsoft Defender.  
 
Customers can use Microsoft Fabric through data mirroring, which is currently in preview and 
planned for general availability around Ignite. Mirroring does not duplicate data and only creates a 
logical connection. Fabric analytics and compute workloads are billed separately based on Fabric 
capacity consumption.  Fabric analytics and compute workloads are billed separately based on 
Fabric capacity consumption. 
 
Licensing, pricing and billing 
 
 
Q37. Does ISOC have commitment tiers? 
A. There are no volume commitment tiers for ISOC. Non-Microsoft data ingestion is billed on a pay-
as-you-go basis at $2.40/GB (U.S. pricing).  
Q38. What happens to the existing Sentinel 5MB benefit for E5 and E7 customers? 
A. The existing 5MB Sentinel benefit for E5/E7 customers remain in place for customers staying on 
Sentinel; when customers opt into ISOC, ISOC benefits replace it. 
Q39. Does the Defender for Servers P2 500 MB/day/server benefit remain? 
A. Yes. The existing 500 MB/day/server Defender for Servers Plan 2 (P2) benefit remains 
unchanged, and Sentinel customers who opt into ISOC will continue to receive it.  
Q40. Is Project Perception included within ISOC benefit? 
A. No, not as licensing entitlement.  
 


--- PAGE 16 ---
Microsoft Confidential | Internal Only 
 
Q41. What happens to a Sentinel customer's pricing, pre-purchase plans and discounts if 
they move to ISOC? 
A. If an eligible Sentinel customer chooses to transition to ISOC, the customer's existing commercial 
terms and discounts will need to be renegotiated as part of that transition. It is advised to work the 
account team before moving to ISOC. 
Q42. How does regional pricing work for ISOC and the built-in data lake? 
A. ISOC uses a simplified regional pricing model to provide more consistent and predictable pricing 
across Azure regions. 
• 
ISOC data ingestion: Uses three regional pricing bands:  
o 
US: Base pricing 
o 
Europe: 20% above US pricing 
o 
Rest of world: 30% above US pricing 
• 
Built-in data lake ingestion, processing, and query: Follows the same three regional 
pricing bands as ISOC data ingestion. 
• 
Data lake storage: Continues to use Azure's existing region-specific storage pricing, 
aligned with Microsoft Fabric OneLake. 
Q43. How can I help my customers estimate their ISOC costs?  
A.  
• 
Leverage this internal excel-based ISOC pricing estimator: https://aka.ms/isocpricing. 
• 
Or use the new external web-based calculator: https://aka.ms/defenderisoccostestimator 
(coming soon, ETA: Nov 23) 
Q44. Does ISOC usage decrement from a customer’s Microsoft Azure Consumption 
Commitment (MACC)? 
A. Yes. 
Q45. Does Microsoft offer a managed service for ISOC in Defender?  
A. Yes. Microsoft Defender Experts MDR is Microsoft’s managed detection and response (MDR) 
service that delivers 24/7 expert-led, AI-accelerated triage, investigation, response, and proactive 
threat hunting. Defender Experts MDR is natively integrated in Defender and helps defend against 
threats across endpoints, identities, emails, cloud apps, cloud workloads, and network, using 
Microsoft and non-Microsoft data sources.  
 
Defender Experts MDR is available in 2 SKUs: Defender Experts MDR P1 and Defender Experts MDR 
P2.  
Q46. What is the difference between Defender Experts MDR P1 and Defender Experts MDR 
P2?  
A.  
• 
Defender Experts MDR P1 is the recommended choice for customers whose security 
operations primarily revolve around first-party data sources in Microsoft Defender.  
• 
Defender Experts MDR P2 includes all MDR P1 capabilities and extends coverage to 
supported non-Microsoft data sources, enabling broader threat detection, investigation, and 


--- PAGE 17 ---
Microsoft Confidential | Internal Only 
 
response across the customer's environment. P2 is intended for customers who need 
protection across both Microsoft and non-Microsoft security environments.  
• 
MDR coverage of hybrid and multi-cloud servers in Microsoft Defender for Cloud is 
available as a separate add-on.  
Q47. What data sources does Defender Experts MDR cover?  
A. Defender Experts MDR P1 covers Microsoft data sources while Defender Experts MDR P2 covers 
both native Microsoft data sources and supported non-Microsoft data sources.   
• 
Endpoints: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint P2, CrowdStrike Falcon EDR*  
• 
Identity Protection: Microsoft Entra ID protection, Microsoft Defender for Identity, Okta, 
CrowdStrike Falcon ITP*   
• 
Email Security: Microsoft Defender for O365 P2, Proofpoint email security, Mimecast*  
• 
Cloud App Security: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, Netskope*  
• 
Cloud infrastructure security: AWS Guard Duty, AWS Cloud Trail, Google Cloud Audit*, 
Wiz*, Palo Alto Prisma*  
• 
Network security and firewalls: Palo Alto PANOS Next-gen Firewall, Cisco ASA/Meraki, 
Zscaler ZIA/ZPA, Fortinet FortiGate, Checkpoint NGFW*, Cloudflare NGFW*  
 
(*Indicates products on roadmap and coming soon) 
Q48. What are the pre-requisites and baseline criteria for Defender Experts MDR?  
A. Defender Experts MDR has a set of onboarding pre-requisites and baseline criteria to initiate 
operations.  
Q49. Where can I find additional FAQs for Defender Experts MDR?  
Refer to the Defender Experts MDR and Hunting Internal FAQ for more frequently asked questions. 
 
Field questions 
 
 
Q49. What should I sell for a new SIEM opportunity? 
A. For new customers with Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft Defender E5, or Microsoft Defender Suite, 
lead with ISOC for SIEM capabilities. 
Q50. What empowerment offers apply to ISOC? 
A.  
• 
Standard Azure discount up to 15% applies to ISOC.  
• 
Current Sentinel empowerment offers do not apply to ISOC. Sentinel Commitment tier 
pricing and negotiated discounts do not carry over to ISOC, so sellers should work with 
Sentinel customers to compare their projected Sentinel and ISOC costs before 
recommending migration. 


--- PAGE 18 ---
Microsoft Confidential | Internal Only 
 
• 
Azure Consumption Discount (ACD) applies to ISOC.  
Q51. How does ISOC help sellers retire more quota? 
A. ISOC helps sellers recognize more security ACR. ISOC expands the conversation from SIEM to full 
security operations transformation, helping customers maximize their existing Microsoft E5 and E7 
and Defender suite investments while enabling larger platform deals. It supports vendor 
consolidation, unlocks budget for agentic security and AI-powered operations, and creates 
opportunities for both immediate revenue growth and long-term security expansion.  
Q51.  How are ISOC meters attributed to Security ACR? 
A. 100% of ISOC revenue will retire quota as Strategic Security ACR within the Sentinel ACR metric. 
There will be no revenue or quota-credit split with Azure Monitoring for ISOC meters. This applies 
to all ISOC meters only; the existing Security/Monitoring split for current Sentinel meters remains 
unchanged. 
Q52. How do sellers create ISOC sales opportunity? 
A. Sellers should create a new pipeline or convert existing Sentinel pipeline using the MSX 
workload Sec: Azure Sec – ISOC. 
Q53. What program offerings are available for ISOC?  
A. To find out what program offerings are available for your ISOC opportunity, submit your 
Opportunity ID at aka.ms/FrontieraccelerateforSecurity.

Part 1. Understand ISOC 
 
1.1 What is ISOC in Microsoft Defender 
ISOC in Microsoft Defender is a benefit that brings together leading SIEM and threat 
protection in an integrated experience for agentic security, giving people and agents a 
shared foundation to see, understand, and act across the environment without the 
complexity of operating separate systems.  
1.2 Customer value 
ISOC brings SIEM capabilities directly into Defender, enabling customers to use Defender 
data without re-ingestion, retain it for 90 days by default, and flexibly extend retention 
and security coverage with 500+ connectors as needs evolve. 


--- PAGE 5 ---
ISOC in Microsoft Defender | Playbook 
This unified foundation of signals, context, and actions enables people and agents to work 
together across security operations, accelerating investigation and response while 
keeping practitioners in control. 
1.3 Eligibility

Microsoft 365 E7. 
• 
Eligible customers without an existing Microsoft Sentinel deployment can start 
using ISOC directly in the Microsoft Defender portal. 
• 
Eligible customers with an existing Microsoft Sentinel deployment can choose to 
transition that deployment to ISOC. Existing Sentinel customers are not 
automatically moved to ISOC. For existing Microsoft Sentinel customers, the 
onboarding journey starts by identifying dependencies, migrating affected 
content and validating outcomes.

2.2 Extend Microsoft Defender data retention 
You can extend retention for supported Microsoft Defender data for 180 days (analytics). 
Extended retention applies to new data after you enable it; data collected before that is 
not backfilled. Beyond 180 days, retain data in the analytics tier for up to two years or use 
long-term retention in the data lake for longer-term analysis, audit, or compliance needs. 
Applicable retention charges apply beyond what is included with ISOC. 
2.3 Additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security data 
An ISOC workspace is required to ingest additional Microsoft and non-Microsoft security 
data through 500+ data connectors. This data is billed at $2.40 per GB (US East) with 90 
days retention included. Regional pricing may vary.

Part 4. Review SOC optimization recommendations 
 
4.1 Before you start 
Connect all Microsoft Sentinel workspaces in your deployment to the Microsoft Defender 
portal and confirm you have the permissions needed to review and update content. SOC 
optimization recommendations can take up to 48 hours to appear after workspace 
onboarding or changes to table retention. 
Treat SOC optimization as your migration worklist. It tells the team which Defender tables 
are candidates for reducing double ingestion costs and which detections, workbooks, 
playbooks, or other resources must be reviewed first. 


--- PAGE 10 ---

1. Sign in to the Microsoft Defender portal and open SOC optimization. 
2. Review the recommendations related to Microsoft Defender data ingestion across 
all connected workspaces. 
3. Identify the tables included in each recommendation. 
4. For each table, identify all content and integrations that depend on the 
corresponding Sentinel data. 
If no recommendation is created for a specific eligible table, there are no assets to 
migrate and ingestion for that table can be reduced immediately. For every other table, 
do not change ingestion until dependencies are reviewed and validated.

Part 5. Update your content 
 
Work through this part in order, for each table family in your backlog. Permissions come 
first, because Sentinel workspace access alone does not grant access to the 
corresponding Defender workload data. 
5.1 Permissions and Unified RBAC 
Use the role import experience in Microsoft Defender Unified RBAC to import supported 
Sentinel roles and assignments, then activate Unified RBAC separately for any required 
Defender workloads that are not already active. Ask your Unified RBAC administrator to 
perform the migration. They need at least the Security Administrator role in Microsoft 
Entra ID (or all Authorization permissions in Unified RBAC), role-management permissions 
across all required scopes, access to the primary Sentinel workspace with authorization to 
onboard it to Unified RBAC, and management access to the Defender workloads to 
include. 
Supported destination workloads are Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Office 365, 
Defender for Identity, and Defender for Cloud Apps. Importing roles does not activate a 
workload, and activating a workload does not import roles. 
To import roles: 
1. In the Microsoft Defender portal, go to System > Permissions, and under 
Microsoft Defender XDR select Roles. 
2. Select Import role. If a banner prompts you to import roles and activate 
workloads, start with the role import. 
3. Confirm Microsoft Sentinel as an import source (the primary workspace is used). 
4. Review the preselected roles, assigned users and groups, permissions, and 
additional data sources. 
5. Submit the import and review the result for each role. Resolve any failures; do not 
reimport roles that succeeded, as this can create duplicates. 
6. Activate Unified RBAC for each required workload that is not already active, then 
review the resulting assignments and scopes. 


--- PAGE 13 ---
ISOC in Microsoft Defender | Playbook 
Before any ingestion change, ask affected users to confirm access, validate permissions 
and scopes for each workload, and review users whose Sentinel access is inherited from 
resource-group or subscription assignments. Restrictions configured in Sentinel are not 
reproduced automatically in Defender. Role import does not migrate application or 
automation permissions, so review automation identities separately. 
Users with only Sentinel permissions may lose visibility into migrated tables, the alerts 
and incidents generated from that data, and custom detections if permissions are not 
migrated. Permission migration is optional for users who already have the required 
Defender access through Unified RBAC or Microsoft Entra ID global roles, together with 
the necessary Sentinel Azure RBAC roles.  
5.2 Update queries to use Advanced Hunting tables 
Most Defender tables have the same name in Sentinel and Advanced Hunting, so table 
references usually do not change. However, some columns and data types work 
differently. For every query, detection, workbook, and playbook you update, replace 
TimeGenerated with Timestamp where applicable, remove dependencies on Sentinel-only 
metadata columns (TenantId, SourceSystem, _IsBillable, _BilledSize), and do not rely on 
MachineGroup for filtering outside DeviceInfo.

5.6 Update UEBA 
After the transition, UEBA processes supported Defender data at the tenant level. Third-
party data continues to reach UEBA through Sentinel data connectors, and UEBA outputs 
continue to be stored in Sentinel workspaces. For a single workspace with existing UEBA, 
the change is seamless and no separate transition is required. 
Do not disable and re-enable UEBA as part of the transition; doing so deletes existing 
profiles and baselines. If you have UEBA-enabled workspaces not yet connected to the 
Defender portal, connect them before the transition and allow 30 days for baselines to 
reaccumulate. 
With multiple workspaces, UEBA output derived from Defender data is written to the 
primary workspace, while output from third-party data stays with the workspace where 
that data is ingested. Onboarding includes an acknowledgment of this change, and 
workspace-specific analytics rules, playbooks, and workbooks that depend on UEBA 
output should be reviewed. Existing DCR filtering does not apply to Defender data used 
directly by UEBA, which might affect processed volume and ingestion charges; there is no 
DCR workaround. 
5.7 Use Content hub 
Content hub, under SIEM > Content management > Content hub, offers a unified 
experience for workspace-level and tenant-level content. Workspace-level content 
requires an ISOC or Sentinel workspace and is installed per workspace. Defender-level 
content (Defender workbooks and custom detections) is deployed at tenant scope 
without a workspace.

plus Deploy permission on the resource group for workspace solutions. Custom 
detections installed from Content hub are read-only and disabled by default: create a 
copy to activate or modify them. Solution updates can overwrite platform-managed 
content but never customer-created copies, and deleting a solution does not delete its 
installed custom detections. 
5.8 Deploy content as code (CI/CD) 
Repository connections, under Microsoft Sentinel > Content management > 
Repositories, deploy content through CI/CD. Workspace-targeted connections support 
existing Sentinel content types (analytics rules, automation rules, custom detection rules, 
hunting queries, parsers, playbooks, and workbooks). Defender XDR (tenant-targeted) 
connections support Defender workbooks and custom detections and do not require a 
workspace. 
The initial setup needs the Global Administrator role in Microsoft Entra ID, and the 
account creating the connection must be in your home tenant; B2B guest accounts and 
delegated access are not supported. GitHub requires Collaborator access with GitHub 
Actions enabled. Azure DevOps support is coming soon. 
After a connection is created, edit content in the repository rather than directly in 
Defender, or your changes might be overwritten on the next deployment. Bicep files 
require a connection created after November 1, 2024.

8.1 Reduce ingestion in controlled waves 
After validation, start with a table whose dependencies are fully validated and whose 
rollback path is understood. You do not need to optimize all tables at once. 
1. Confirm the migration backlog for the table is complete and no active rule, 
workbook, playbook, UEBA dependency, or report still requires Sentinel ingestion. 
2. In the Azure portal, open your Microsoft Sentinel workspace and select 
Configuration > Tables. 
3. Select the table (for example, DeviceNetworkEvents), then select Data retention 
settings. 
4. Set Analytics retention to 30 days (included in license) and select Save.

8.2 Retention exceptions and timing 
If a table uses a retention value that is unsupported during the preview, such as 120 days, 
change it to a supported value before onboarding. If you need retention beyond the 
included 90 days, extend Defender data retention up to 180 days (additional charges 
apply) or keep the table in Sentinel and document the exception. Changes to table 
retention can take up to 48 hours to appear in SOC optimization. 
8.3 Monitor after reducing ingestion 
Monitor over several detection and automation runs. Confirm custom detections, hunting 
queries, workbook tiles, and Logic App playbooks continue to work, and that users and 
automation identities retain access. If something does not behave as expected, review its 
Advanced Hunting table mapping, schema, permissions, and query configuration before 
transitioning additional tables. 
8.4 Repeat table by table 
For each table: identify dependent content, update it to use Advanced Hunting, validate 
queries, detections, workbooks, automation, and access, reduce ingestion, monitor, and 
continue with the next table. This approach prevents coverage gaps throughout the 
transition.

9.2 Frequently asked questions 
Where should we start? Start in the Microsoft Defender portal in SOC optimization, and 
use it to identify eligible Defender tables and dependent content. 
Do all Sentinel analytics rules need to move? No. Only rules that depend on eligible 
Defender tables being removed from ingestion need review, and some rules should 
remain in Sentinel. 
Is 90 days of retention guaranteed for everything? No. Treat 90 days of included 
retention as the target experience for applicable Defender data and validate support by 
data source and tenant state. 
Can we still use workbooks? Yes. Affected tiles should query Defender data through 
Advanced Hunting, and users must have the required underlying data access. 
Can we reduce ingestion before validation? No. Reducing ingestion too early can 
break detections, workbooks, playbooks, hunting, UEBA, reports, and analyst workflows. 
What if a dependency cannot migrate yet? Keep the table ingested in Sentinel, 
document the blocker, assign an owner, and revisit when support or remediation is 
available. 
Is Microsoft threat intelligence ingestion free of charge with ISOC? During the 
Private Preview, ingestion of Microsoft threat intelligence continues to be billed under 
your existing Sentinel threat intelligence terms. It will be included at no additional cost 
starting with ISOC Public Preview. 
We have another tenant with Microsoft Sentinel data lake enabled. Can it be 
onboarded to ISOC? Microsoft Sentinel data lake is currently not supported with ISOC; 
the tenant must offboard from the data lake first. Offboarding permanently deletes all 


--- PAGE 24 ---
ISOC in Microsoft Defender | Playbook 
customer data and compute artifacts (such as jobs and queries), deprovisions all data lake 
storage and compute, and cannot be reversed. Customers can use the data lake tier 
included with ISOC going forward. Offboarding is currently performed by engineering: 
raise a support case through the support portal or work with your Customer Success 
Account Manager (CSAM). 
What evidence should we keep? Keep an evidence pack for each table: SOC 
optimization recommendation, dependency list, updated content links, validation result, 
known exceptions, owner, and date.
